summary: The note explains the phrase "51st state", which can be used positively to describe a region so aligned and supportive of the United States that it is like a U.S. state. It can also be used pejoratively to describe an area perceived to be under excessive American cultural or military influence or control. People in various countries who feel their culture has become too Americanized sometimes apply the term to their own nations.
one_line: Explains the phrase "51st state", used positively for U.S.-aligned regions and pejoratively for areas seen as under excessive American influence.
key_facts: The phrase "51st state" can be used in a positive sense.
In the positive sense, a region or territory is so aligned, supportive, and conducive with the United States that it is like a U.S. state.
In the pejorative sense, the phrase means an area or region is perceived to be under excessive American cultural or military influence or control.
People in various countries who believe their local or national culture has become too Americanized sometimes use the term "51st state" in reference to their own countries.
The term is used around the world in reference to various countries.
The phrase is named for the idea of a fifty-first state added to the United States beyond the existing fifty states.
